title: Docs overhaul: migration paths & usage patterns for tokens, interactive buttons, table kits, and chart primitives
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Replace the scattered, outdated component docs with a single, pragmatic reference that covers token semantics, button states/variants, recommended table usage patterns, and chart primitives. The goal is to reduce onboarding questions, lower incorrect API usage in product repos, and provide clear migration steps for teams moving from legacy tokens and undocumented table props. Scope: update docs site pages, Storybook stories, migration notes, code examples, and add a compact-run checklist for engineering rollouts. Out of scope: making runtime API changes or changing existing visual CSS tokens (this ticket documents migration; implementation PRs are tracked in dependent ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Docs site has new canonical pages: Tokens Guide, Button Patterns, Table Kit Usage, Chart Primitives
Each page includes at least one live Storybook story and a runnable code example that passes TypeScript checks
Migration guide lists mappings from legacy tokens to new tokens and a codemod example (jest + ts-morph)
Two consumer apps (dashboard and console) successfully apply the migration checklist with no visual regressions reported
Doc pages include do/don't examples and an 'When to use' section for each component
PRs merged for documentation updates and Storybook deployment succeeded to staging docs.redwood-inference.com/docs-preview
migration_steps: Inventory: run token-usage-scan across monorepo to generate usage map (ENG-3012 assigned)
Map: create canonical mapping table from legacy tokens to new tokens and publish as spreadsheet in Drive
Codemod: author a targeted codemod for color and spacing tokens and validate on a small app branch
Docs: publish migration guide with step-by-step checklist and expected visual diffs
Rollout: enable deprecation banner in Storybook and announce 3-week migration window before soft deprecation
Follow-up: collect feedback and open follow-up fixes as separate design tickets for edge cases
do_dont_examples: Do: use token references (spacing.x4) in component props so spacing stays responsive
Don't: hardcode px values for margins inside components that should be token-driven
Do: prefer Button variant='primary' and semantic props (loading, disabled) over custom class toggles
Don't: layer click handlers and visual state manipulation in parent when Button has specialized API
Do: use Table.RowKey and Table.Sections for accessibility-first semantics; add aria labels explicitly
Don't: use deprecated Table.pagination props; follow the new PaginationKit examples instead
Do: use Chart primitives for axes and annotate important series with the provided Label component
Don't: embed axis labels into SVG via manual transforms when using Chart primitives — use the API's label props
api_notes: Buttons: no runtime prop removal in this ticket; docs highlight new recommended props: variant, intent, size, loading, tone
Table: document new pagination API and required changes for server-side pagination prop names
Tokens: list breaking token name mappings and note alias behavior (legacy token names will map to new tokens for 3 releases)
Charts: note that Chart.Axis.label API gains a 'wrap' boolean; docs show polyfill pattern for older consumers
